data.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?

result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password or Bitwarden**\.

My overall pick is **1Password if ease of use and team collaboration matter most; Bitwarden if keeping costs down is the priority.**

A business password manager is worth having even with only 3–5 employees. It gives you secure shared credentials, individual user accounts, controlled access and the ability to revoke access when someone leaves.

## My top 4 recommendations

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password**

(Best overall)

- Excellent, polished apps across devices.
- Shared vaults for teams and departments.
- Granular permissions and access controls.
- Security alerts and admin reporting.
- Teams Starter Pack: US\$24.95/month for up to 10 people.
  
  Best for teams wanting something easy to adopt and manage.
  
  [1Password Business](https://1password.com/business)

---

![Free High-Quality Bitwarden Logo for Creative Design](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/p0IJzf2NCUQ2t02rqtPWDpe7Tx4YGCRNleASv1NjpztaDI--7OD-0zWJhdBi_4Wn4-v0Hr3hoS6JA2KXHdCOlvvdfHelZm6tTBmFuxgAbBftLkdqobRCpEkp4ysyI4Rm6vafJPMfHi8ri9Tdeng_QKXRw7C7a5ESA6hn8XLhRMLnvM7oFmwZESsO4_SFLJaX?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden**

(Best value)

- Open-source password manager.
- Shared collections for team credentials.
- Admin controls and event logs.
- Cross-platform apps and browser extensions.
- Teams plan: approximately US\$4/user/month.
  
  Best if you want strong functionality without spending much.
  
  [Bitwarden Business](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

- Strong administrative controls.
- Shared folders and secure credential storage.
- Good options for compliance-focused businesses.
- Business plans start around US\$2/user/month.
  
  Best for businesses wanting structured access management.
  
  [Keeper Business](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

---

![Test Proton Pass Plus - Gestionnaire de mots de passe - Que Choisir Ensemble](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/ieWxaf1V1oKwR5RRYZyCUPTssuPFmf3KGImAFxDImLo918b9HrqSkmcFxYOmTtZlPSYlBfMDN2fRfrT9cxgSPcskegAU9CMbarL_OHz9CIE3qqDdr6RF19eJVNxO2Ol4ntEKr3D7ZAQzGf8y8YfFA_bGj9p5D2RwqWU6uGCUEvGwoAX0vUa7O4BZUHkNpExF?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Proton Pass**

- Privacy-focused approach.
- Secure password sharing.
- Email aliases and additional privacy features.
- Business plans available.
  
  Best for teams that place a high priority on privacy.
  
  [Proton Pass for Business](https://proton.me/business/pass)

Pricing is indicative, in USD, generally billed annually before tax. Confirm current Australian pricing and plan features before purchasing. [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[cybercred.com.au](https://cybercred.com.au/articles/password-managers-compared-for-small-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[itsecureops.com](https://itsecureops.com/guides/small-business-password-managers/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd look for in a small business

Regardless of which product you choose, make sure it supports\:

1. **Shared vaults\:** Store company logins in a central place.
2. **Individual accounts\:** Everyone has their own login.
3. **Permission management\:** Staff only see credentials they need.
4. **Easy offboarding\:** Revoke access immediately when someone leaves.
5. **Two-factor authentication\:** Protect access to the password manager itself.
6. **Audit logs\:** Know who accessed or changed shared credentials.

## My recommendation

I'd shortlist 1Password and Bitwarden and trial both before committing.

## A couple of questions

I can narrow this down considerably with two details\:

**How many people are on your team?**
